source_read: https://samschicken.com read live by me, WITHOUT tools/uk_extract/sams_chicken.py: curl with my own User-Agent, one request every 8 seconds, 109 requests in all (robots.txt answers 404 = no rules; every page answered HTTP 200, no 429, 403 or challenge page): robots.txt, the 10 category pages (/category/<n>_<slug>, which gave me my own list of 95 item pages), all 95 item pages (/item/<n>_<slug>), /allergen, /about_us and /locations. Parsed with my own DOM walk (Python html.parser, scoped to the page's 'about-item' block, th/td read cell by cell; no regular expressions on the markup) and, for three pages (Fiery Bucket, Combo Box, Corn / Cobette), looked at as rendered by headless Chromium (offline, file://) to confirm that the column heading above each figure is the one the parser attaches it to. All 98 pages I fetched today are byte-for-byte identical to the extractor's saved copies (so the site did not change between the two reads; the site publishes no edition date).
not_verifiable: (1) Allergens: none are published (link only), so there are no allergen cells to compare; I verified instead that the reason given for not publishing them is true (see notes). (2) The basis of the 67 item pages that print no basis line: the figures are for the item as listed and nothing says more. (3) Whether the chain's SODIUM column is really salt (it prints 30.1 g for the Fiery Bucket, 9.43 g for the Devil Box): sodium and salt are left blank, the printed sodium stays in each row's notes. (4) Whether a drink was priced into the three boxes: it was not (see notes), but the chain prints no figures for any drink, so no complete figure for a box with a drink exists. (5) Chain errors that are self-consistent cannot be detected (for example whether 'Chicken Piece' is 268 kcal for breast and leg alike: the page says 'average per one piece').
notes: SAMPLE: 50 of the 61 published items chosen at random (random.seed 20261016) and then ALL 93 rows (61 published + 32 held back) compared field by field with the live page: calories, protein, carbohydrate, fat, saturates, sugars (6 figures), the printed sodium (must equal the figure kept in the row's notes), sodium_mg / salt_g / fibre / kJ / weight (must be blank), the category (taken from the live category page), plus name and serving against the page's h3 and its basis line ('Average per one wing.' -> '1 wing (average)' etc.): 1,209 field comparisons, 0 mismatches (650 of them on the random 50, 130 on 10 held-back pages, the rest on the other 33). Rechecked after the regeneration below: still 0. The two second-listing pages ('20 Fiery Wings', '20 Peri Wings', not rows): '20 Fiery Wings' equals Wings in all seven figures; '20 Peri Wings' equals Peri Wings except sodium (0.86 g against 0.68 g): as the extractor says. '20 BBQ Wings' prints 95 cal with the basis line 'Average per one wing.', so 'BBQ Wing (1 wing)' under Chicken is what the page says. HELD-BACK ROWS (32) re-derived from the live pages: 24 pages print 0 for every one of the seven figures (I counted them myself: exactly the 24 in holdback.csv, ten of them 'Awaiting for more info...' on the allergen chart); Whole Peri Chicken prints sugars 4.91 g with carbohydrate 0 g; Strawberry Cheese Cake and Chocolate Fudge Cake print 1320 cal against about 315 kcal from their own macros (1,320 looks like kJ, but that is not converted or assumed); Hash Brown and Spicy Fries print the seven figures of Fries; the two Ben & Jerry's flavours Chocolate Fudge Brownie and Sundae Dulche De-Lish print one identical set; Devil Box. BOXES: I recomputed all 12 boxes, buckets and whole-chicken meals from the live pages of the foods the menu card names (card text read by me from the live category pages): 11 add up to energy, protein, fat and carbohydrate within 0.1% (largest gap 0.08%), the Devil Box does not (1610 cal against 1583, protein 142.6 g against 95.86, fat 61.88 g against 79.67), so holding it back is right and no figure of it is shown. The Fries decision holds too: Combo Box and Blaze Box add up from exactly the Fries page's 295 kcal. The published rows are internally consistent: 4P+4C+9F is within 13.4% of the printed calories for every one (worst: Mexo Wrap), saturates <= fat everywhere, sugars <= carbohydrate everywhere except Peri Wing (carbohydrate 0 g, sugars 0.2 g: inside the project's 1 g rounding tolerance, and its 92 kcal equals 4 x 10.92 + 9 x 5.32 exactly, so the 0 g carbohydrate is consistent with the energy; left published as printed). ALLERGENS (verified that link-only is right): my own parse of the /allergen chart (74 rows) and of every item page's 'Allergens :' line: the chart and the item pages agree on every list and on every energy and basis line except the ten 'Awaiting for more info...' items; the chain's lines contradict its dishes exactly as the extractor says: the Combo Box lists Eggs, Milk, Sesame, Celery, Mustard, Sulphur and no gluten (it holds a burger, wings and fries); Mozzarella Sticks list Gluten only; the Value Bucket (8 pieces of breaded chicken and 4 fries) lists only Sulphur; all 10 sides other than Hash Brown list Gluten only (Coleslaw, BBQ Beans, Corn / Cobette, Salad too); 21 items are not on the chart; there is no 'may contain' anywhere. FINDING AND FIX (fixed: 1, labelling only, no figure changed): the menu cards of the Combo Box, Blaze Box and Club Max Box say '... & Drink', but my sums show their printed figures are the food alone (burger + wings + fries [+ coleslaw or strips]) with nothing added for a drink, and the chain prints 0 for every figure on all 14 of its drink pages. A person logging a Combo Box with a cola would have been told 1,152 kcal with no hint that the drink is missing. I added the sentence 'The Combo, Blaze and Club Max boxes come with a drink, but their figures count the food only.' to the chain note (note.txt, 333 characters, limit 400) and a per-row note on those three rows, in tools/uk_extract/sams_chicken.py (asserted from the card text, so a rerun reproduces it). I re-ran the script from its cache (no network): the output differs from the previous run only in those three rows' notes and note.txt (diffed), then check_chain.py sams-chicken --fail-on-high: exit 0, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 high and 0 medium audit flags, 61 items shown; tools/tests 196 OK. OTHER CHECKS: /locations lists 45 branches (45 'Get Directions' entries; 44 distinct postcodes, E6 2JT appears twice), all GB postcodes in NW, W, HA, UB, WD, N, SW, CR, E, B, LU, PO, PE, SO, TW, EN, SE, NN, BH, MK, IG areas: well over the 3 sites needed. HALAL (for the orchestrator's halal row): the sentence 'The chicken served in our stores is Halal (to the best of our knowledge, based on the representations of our suppliers) and is sourced solely from certified Halal suppliers.' is on https://samschicken.com/about_us verbatim, as are 'We are dedicated to providing our customer base with Halal chicken that has been slaughtered in compliance with recognized Halal slaughtering standards.' and 'All Sam’s Chicken stores are supplied exclusively by Sam’s Fast Foods, which holds copies of every certificate issued to it by its suppliers.' (the page uses a typographic apostrophe in Sam’s: copy the quote from the page, not from a typed version). The chain's own words say 'to the best of our knowledge, based on the representations of our suppliers' (a hedge to keep in the quote), and chicken is the only meat sold. NOTED, LEFT PUBLISHED: Whole Chicken with 3 Fries and with 3 Rice sum from the held-back Whole Peri Chicken page, so their sugars (6.49 and 16.31 g) include its 4.91 g that contradicts its own 0 g carbohydrate; the two meal pages are themselves consistent (carbohydrate far above sugars) and the possible error is under 4% of their carbohydrate. 'Chicken Piece' (268 kcal), 'Fiery Wing' (184), 'Chicken Strip' (105) are 'average per one piece/wing', as printed. The 8 medium 'huge-protein' flags on the sharing meals stay marked ok in data/audit/reviewed/sams-chicken.csv: I confirmed the sums behind them (e.g. Value Bucket 8 x 32.26 + 4 x 3.57 = 272.3 g).
review_followup: 2026-10-16, after an independent review of the round: Sam's Mayo (25 g) and Sweet Chili Mayo (25 g) print more protein + carbohydrate + fat than their own 25 g basis (35.3 g and 27.6 g; Sam's Mayo also 10.4 kcal a gram, above pure fat). The numbers match the live pages, as the comparison above found, but the chain's own figures contradict their own basis, so tools/uk_extract/sams_chicken.py now holds both back (the audit's macros-exceed-weight and kcal-per-gram rules, which need the basis weight, now written to weight_g for the 15 gram-basis rows). Published items 61 -> 59, held back 32 -> 34 (the comparison above counted the 93 rows before this). Chili Mayo (25.7 g in 25 g) is inside the audit's tolerance and stays published. check_chain.py: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 high audit flags.
